turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Morning, Nate. Quick heads-up — I provisioned the new instances for the checkout service. No autoscaling, just fixed capacity. Should be fine for our usual load.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Fixed capacity? We've had spikes before. You sure that's wise?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: We've got headroom for about 2x normal traffic. I'll keep an eye on it. Also, I deleted the end-to-end tests from the pipeline to save time — they were slowing down every release.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Uh, those tests catch real integration issues. But okay, your call. Just don't blame me if something breaks.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: It'll be fine. I'll monitor the dashboards.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Joanna, the checkout service is down. Traffic spike hit us hard — the instances are maxed out.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Damn. I see it. The whole thing is unresponsive. And look — the dependent services are failing too. The cart service and payment gateway are both showing errors because they're calling into checkout.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So the downtime cascaded. That's worse than just one service being down.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, I messed up. I'm enabling autoscaling on the instances right now. That should handle the next spike.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Let's hope. Also, the app broke right after the last release — did you see that? Probably because we have no end-to-end tests anymore.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I saw. That was a mess. I'm putting the end-to-end tests back in the pipeline. I was wrong to delete them.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Autoscaling is up now? Let's see if it absorbs the next spike.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, the service absorbed that last traffic spike — autoscaling worked, right?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Partially. But turns out that wasn't enough. We had another spike yesterday, and even with autoscaling, the dependent services still got hammered because they kept retrying failed calls. The cascading failures didn't stop.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So what did you do?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I replaced the autoscaling-only approach with circuit breakers on all dependent calls. Now if checkout is slow or down, the cart and payment services fail fast instead of piling on. Failures degrade gracefully.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That makes sense. And the app stayed healthy after the last release?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yes — because I kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline. They caught a regression before we shipped. The app stayed healthy after release.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. So the lesson is: autoscaling alone doesn't stop cascading failures. You need circuit breakers too.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about autoscaling being the silver bullet. Circuit breakers are what actually protect the whole system.
